body:
# Crypto stocks: how to analyze crypto companies

Crypto stocks swing far harder than the stock market at large — Coinbase's beta of 3.39 means the share has on average moved three and a half times wider than the market. Yet a crypto stock is entirely different from a crypto asset: it is a company whose revenues, balance sheet or earnings are tied to the crypto market's cycles. This guide teaches how three business models differ, where revenue quality is decided, which accounting trap hides in the balance sheet and what the MiCA rules mean — Coinbase runs through it all.

## Three business models in crypto stocks

Crypto companies come in three main forms, whose risk pictures differ as much between them as against the rest of the market.

- **The exchange and the platform.** Coinbase runs a trading platform earning commission on trading volumes, complemented by custody, USDC interest and services. Platforms live on trust and liquidity — more traders mean better prices, creating the [network effects](/kurser/v15-natverkseffekter) that concentrate the sector around few players. Since the April 2021 listing Coinbase has grown to around 4,950 employees — a service organization with a fixed cost base, amplifying the earnings swings both ways.
- **The holding company.** Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) is the world's largest listed corporate bitcoin holder: more than 845,000 BTC at the end of August 2026, over 3 percent of the 21 million bitcoin that can ever be created, at an average cost around 75,400 dollars per coin per the purchase history. The purchases are financed by issuing shares and debt instruments, stacking capital structure risk on top of the price exposure. The operations are in practice the balance sheet — the share is leverage on the bitcoin price, not on a business.
- **The mining operation.** Marathon Digital (MARA) and peers earn block rewards and transaction fees with computers and electricity. Revenue follows block rewards, power costs and machine investments — a capital-intensive craft where the network's halvings build in revenue drops: when the reward halved in April 2024 it fell to 3.125 bitcoin per block — same machines, half as many new coins per day.

## Revenue quality: transaction or subscription

The first question in any crypto company analysis is how its revenues are composed. Transaction revenues — fees on trading — swing with the volumes: when prices rise, more is traded; when they fall, trading thins out. Subscription and service revenues, such as custody and interest on stablecoins, recur and dampen the swings.

Coinbase shows the dynamics in numbers. Trailing twelve months to September 2026, revenue was 6.04 billion dollars, down 9.2 percent, and net income landed at minus 987.8 million. Full-year 2025: the same company at 6.88 billion in revenue, up 9.4 percent, and a positive result of 1.26 billion. Same company, twelve months apart — the difference lies in how volume-sensitive the revenues are, while the cost base stands still. The method for separating cash-generating operations from accounting profit is in the [cash flow analysis](/kurser/km-003-kassaflodesanalysen).

## The balance sheet and the accounting trap

At many crypto companies the largest asset is the crypto itself — and there the accounting standard makes the difference. Under US GAAP, crypto assets have since December 2023 been carried at fair value, with changes through the income statement (FASB ASU 2023-08): when the price rises the profit bubbles up; when it falls, the result is dragged down. Under IFRS, crypto is usually an intangible asset under IAS 38 — impairment when prices fall, normally no write-up when they rise.

The consequence matters pedagogically: two companies with identical holdings can report different profits just because they follow different standards, and the result swings for accounting reasons even when operations are unchanged. Strategy is the extreme case — the balance sheet is in essence the bitcoin holding, turning the quarterly report into a mirror of the prices. Always read the notes and the standard before interpreting the profit, as in the [quarterly report](/kurser/km-006-kvartalsrapporten).

## Crypto stocks in numbers — a worked example

Concrete key ratios for Coinbase, closing price 17 September 2026: share price 173.97 dollars, market capitalization 45.9 billion. The trailing twelve-month net margin came to minus 16.4 percent (minus 987.8 million divided by 6,040 million) against plus 18.3 percent for full-year 2025 — a swing of nearly 35 percentage points within a year. The share traded between 139 and 402 dollars over 52 weeks, roughly 57 percent below the peak. Behind all of it stands the beta of 3.39: the share has on average moved more than three times wider than the index — explaining both the range and how one vote in the US Congress can move the market capitalization by billions in a day.

The multiple tells the rest: a forward P/E of around 165, because the market prices an earnings turnaround, while trailing P/E cannot be calculated at all — the result is negative. That is the position for many crypto stocks: valuation rests on expectations, not realized profits, and small changes in the figures move the price sharply. The tool for measuring it is the course on [volatility and standard deviation](/kurser/km-013-volatilitet-standardavvikelse).

## Regulation: MiCA, Finansinspektionen and the Swedish Tax Agency

Since 30 December 2024 the EU's crypto regulation MiCA (Regulation (EU) 2023/1114) has applied. It divides the assets into e-money tokens, asset-referenced tokens and other crypto assets, and requires crypto service providers to be authorized, warn customers about risks and make suitability assessments whenever advice is given. Finansinspektionen, the Swedish financial supervisory authority, has with EU colleagues repeatedly reminded that the rulebook does not remove the risks — nor are all assets covered.

Regulation is also a revenue factor, not just paperwork: when the US Senate in September 2026 voted down the crypto legislation Clarity Act, Coinbase fell around 9 percent in one day. Weaving such [regulatory risk](/kurser/rk-06-regulatorisk-risk) into the analysis is a step of its own. For private individuals in Sweden, the Swedish Tax Agency's (Skatteverket) rules also apply: gains are taxed at 30 percent, losses are deductible at 70 percent, and a disposal occurs even when crypto is exchanged for a good — the events are reported in the K4 form. From 2027, crypto service providers must also report customers' transactions to the Swedish Tax Agency under the DAC8 rules, raising transparency in the tax returns.

## Three checks in the analysis

- **The revenue split.** How much of the revenues is volume-dependent fees, and how much is recurring services? The larger the transaction share, the harder the result swings with the cycle.
- **The balance sheet and the standard.** How much of the assets is crypto, which standard applies, and how are value changes treated — fair value or impairment?
- **The regulatory position.** Is the operation authorized in its jurisdictions, and when is the next report due? Coinbase reports next quarter on 29 October 2026 — the date itself is a risk event.

## The summary

- Three models: the platform lives on commission revenue, the holding company on bitcoin in the balance sheet, the miner on block rewards minus electricity and machines — same sector, three different risks.
- Revenue quality: Coinbase went from a net margin of plus 18.3 percent in 2025 to minus 16.4 percent twelve months later — volume sensitivity is the sector's signature.
- Accounting: fair value under US GAAP versus impairment under IFRS means the same price swing gives different profit figures — read the notes before the profit.
- Regulation: MiCA authorizes and warns, Finansinspektionen repeats the risks, and the Swedish Tax Agency taxes gains at 30 percent with loss deductions at 70 percent.
- Valuation: forward multiples around 165 on a negative result show the price rests on expectations — the beta of 3.39 measures the swings.

The continuation track: [The crypto sector](/kurser/se-11-krypto) deepens every theme of this guide, and [the complete guide to Swedish stock analysis](/blogg/komplett-guide-svensk-aktieanalys-2026) puts the method in context.
